body:
Good morning, Bakersfield. It’s Friday, August 21, 2026, and we’re waking up to a day that will reach about 101°, with air quality at a moderate 93. Overnight, a semi truck fully engulfed on northbound I-5 south of Grapevine kept crews working for hours, and a fast-moving brush fire on McCombs Road north of Wasco drew a heavy fire response. Let’s get you caught up on the night, the weather, and what’s making news in Kern County.

## The Kern Overnight

The night’s most significant incident was a semi truck and trailer that became fully engulfed on northbound I-5 south of Grapevine just before 1 a.m. CHP and Engine 56 were on scene, and by 6 a.m. crews were still working the fire, with a heavy-duty tow called in and traffic backing up to the Lebec service route. Earlier in the evening, around 10:34 p.m., a quarter-acre brush fire on McCombs Road north of Wasco was burning with a fast rate of spread and potential to run west. Multiple engines and a water tender responded, with additional wildland equipment ordered for what command described as a lengthy mop-up. 

Elsewhere, around 3 a.m., two subjects were reported on a Woodford Boulevard property behind a white pickup, possibly taking items. The subjects were known to be in possession of firearms, though none were visible at first; officers later made contact and located a firearm. And around 9:50 p.m., a robbery at gunpoint was reported on Denise Avenue in north Bakersfield. The suspect was described as a transient white male in his late 30s, wearing a baseball cap and black face mask, pulling a wagon, and accompanied by a white female. 

Finally, around 4:36 a.m., three subjects at a trucking yard south of Gibson Street were reported possibly taking items. Deputies set a perimeter and the subjects ran — one headed south toward a fence with an officer holding the hole. One subject was described as known to carry a knife.

## Today's weather

We’re in for a hot one today with a high near 101° and a low around 74° tonight. It’s already 97° at Meadows Field (KBFL) as of this morning. There are no active weather alerts for Kern County, and air quality is holding at a moderate 93. Stay cool and hydrated out there.

## Top stories

**KGET 17 reports that Flood Ministries has been providing support to Kern County families for two decades, marking a significant milestone in their mission to foster hope and stability within the community.** This long-standing commitment to service highlights the positive impact of their efforts over the years. 

**23ABC tells us that the California Highway Patrol has confirmed new details in the deadly Highway 99 crash from early Sunday morning.** CHP confirmed the BMW involved in the crash was the vehicle traveling northbound in the southbound lanes at the time of the collision. All other aspects of the crash remain under investigation, including potential charges. 

**According to 23ABC, NAMI Kern County will celebrate its 20th annual 'NAMIWalks' this October at the Park at Riverwalk.** The annual event aims to connect our local community members with resources for themselves or their loved ones who may be struggling with their mental health. 

**23ABC also reports that a former Foothill High School student is heading to his dream school after being awarded a $25,000 scholarship.** Eric Ventura was awarded the California Table Grape Scholarship after applying last October. After months of waiting, he learned he won the $25,000 award, which will be spread across his four years at UC Berkeley.

## Something good

It’s always heartening to see our community come together to support those in need. Flood Ministries has been providing support to Kern County families for two decades, marking a significant milestone in their mission to foster hope and stability within the community. This long-standing commitment to service highlights the positive impact of their efforts over the years. 

## Coming up this week

Looking ahead, there are several public meetings and events worth noting. On Wednesday, August 26, the Bakersfield City Council will hold a Special City Council Meeting at 12:00 p.m., followed by a City Council Meeting at 3:30 p.m. and another at 5:15 p.m. 

On the entertainment front, the Fox Theater has a busy week ahead. Tonight, Friday, August 21, Los Yonic's Zamacona, Los caminantes, y Grupo Yndio will perform. On Tuesday, August 25, the Cults & Classics: Season Pass 2026-2027 goes on sale. Comedian Rodney Carrington takes the stage on Thursday, August 27. The Cumbia Rave, CUMBIATRON, is set for Friday, August 28. And on Saturday, August 29, you can catch Willie Barcena or the Michael Return Of The King Tribute Featuring Michael Phoenix. 

That’s your Friday morning brief. Stay cool, stay safe, and have a great weekend.
